details.description:
Huge giant

GM: A rare, hulking troll with a second head that bites twice as often. Use fire or acid from the first round.

Solo: Giant or golem. A normal creature of its Level unless the GM runs it as a solo (tick Run as solo before the fight). As a solo: it fights in three phases with this HP in each; at 0 HP its next phase starts at full HP (damage beyond 0 is lost) and every condition and hostile effect on it ends; at its first phase change only, its breath weapons and other limited-use abilities recover (never spells); once a round, so for the rest of a round in which it changed phase damage can't take it below 1 HP; at 0 HP in its third phase it dies (all automatic). It acts twice a round, on its initiative and again 10 lower (the second turn repeats its attacks, never a spell or limited ability). Villain actions: the giant or golem type's three (in its abilities, worked out for its Level); the opener straight after the first enemy turn, the crowd control after the turn that starts its second phase, the ultimate after the turn that starts its third; it skips its second turn in a round it uses one, if that turn is still to come. Anything that stops it acting, attacking, moving or casting, or banishes, imprisons or petrifies it, ends after two of its turns (one, the second time in a fight), then nothing of the kind affects it until the end of the following round. A kill effect deals damage equal to its current HP (yours to apply). Area, aura and ongoing damage come once a round, at the start of its first turn.

As a normal creature: its HP once, one turn a round, no villain actions and no shaking it off. Its breath weapons, spells and other powers that hit more than one creature deal half damage; it also halves its attack damage.
details.treasure: Treasure type R, lair C (see the Treasure tables).

system.description: Advantage on Perception checks and on saves against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned or knocked unconscious.

Regains 10 HP at the start of its first turn each round.

  • If reduced to 0 HP by anything other than fire or acid damage, it falls prone and rises again at the start of its next turn instead of dying; fire or acid damage stops the regeneration until the end of its next turn.
  • A creature can drop a lit torch or flask of oil on a fallen troll as its object use; that counts as fire, and a troll burned this way stays dead.

Each creature within 30ft makes a @Check[fort|dc:19]{Fortitude save DC 19} or falls @Condition[prone]{Prone}, taking @Damage[2d6 bludgeoning]{2d6 bludgeoning damage}.

A giant or golem solo's opener (Running a Solo, Monsters & Treasure). Every rider lasts until the end of the target's next turn.

It sweeps everything within its reach (at least 15ft). Each creature there makes a @Check[ref|dc:19]{Reflex save DC 19}, taking @Damage[4d6 bludgeoning]{4d6 bludgeoning damage}, being pushed 10ft and falling @Condition[prone]{Prone} on a failure, or half damage on a success.

A giant or golem solo's crowd control (Running a Solo, Monsters & Treasure). Every rider lasts until the end of the target's next turn.

It moves up to its speed in a straight line; each creature in its path makes a @Check[ref|dc:19]{Reflex save DC 19} or falls @Condition[prone]{Prone}.

  • It then makes its full attack line against one creature at the end.
  • If any attack hits, the target is pushed 15ft and falls @Condition[prone]{Prone}.

A giant or golem solo's ultimate (Running a Solo, Monsters & Treasure). Every rider lasts until the end of the target's next turn.
